lines: Anything a rider, a bike or a browser sends is data. Telo Ride checks it on the way in, and shows it as text on the way out.
Every request now has a validator. Ids keep the catalogue's shape, power stays between zero and two thousand watts, and nothing counts below zero.
Break a rule, or send text where a number belongs, and the answer is 400, validation failed, naming the field. No dot-net type name leaks out.
The ride hub refuses the same way: a power reading of minus five watts comes back as validation failed, power watts.
A bike whose name holds markup pairs, and its name shows character for character. Nothing in it runs.
And lint now refuses every way round that: no inner HTML binding, and no bypassing Angular's sanitiser.
Connect Bike, from a phone to the full screen.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
